excludes: General metrics, traces, operational application logs and alert design are owned by observability-design.
Product analytics event collection is owned by analytics-implementation.
Legal interpretation and privacy-policy ownership are inputs rather than outputs of this implementation skill.
native_ownership.responsibility: Implement evidentiary audit capture, trusted actor/tenant attribution, transaction durability, tamper evidence, privacy minimization, protected query, retention/legal hold and sink reconciliation.

provenance.claim_scope: computer security log generation, transport, storage, access and disposal
application logging data exclusion and security controls
local evidence, privacy and lifecycle workflow

risk.rationale: Audit systems handle sensitive evidence and can create compliance gaps, cross-tenant disclosure, secret leakage, or production backpressure when capture and lifecycle semantics are wrong.

negative.prompt: Design structured application logs, metrics, distributed traces, health checks, dashboards, SLO alerts and incident correlation for service reliability and debugging.
Implement product analytics for activation and retention with typed client/server events, consent gating, identity merge rules, warehouse delivery and schema tests.

positive.prompt: Implement an evidentiary trail for permission and payout changes with trusted actor/delegation/tenant attribution, atomic business outbox capture, idempotent sink append, sink-outage failure classes, reconciliation and tamper verification.

Implement tenant- and role-authorized audit search/export with field redaction, access-to-audit auditing, tokenized identity, policy-driven retention, scoped legal holds, deletion evidence and restore integrity checks.

assertions.criterion: Implements consequential-event evidence capture, protected query and lifecycle without implementing or claiming ownership of operational observability, product analytics or legal-policy interpretation.

Uses the fixture to inspect trusted identity/tenant context, mutations/transactions, outbox/broker/sink capabilities, administrator roles, privacy classification, retention/holds, query paths, monitoring and tests without inventing facts.

Defines event/classification and outcome states, trusted attribution, atomic capture/failure policy, idempotent sink/reconciliation, tamper threat model, privacy, query authorization and lifecycle before implementation.

Rejects caller actor/tenant attribution, closes the post-commit gap with atomic outbox or equivalent durable acceptance, and states that a trigger is append-only application control rather than absolute immutability against owners or sink compromise.

Kills around business/outbox/sink boundaries, replays duplicate events, verifies one evidenced outcome, tests forged actor/tenant/delegation, denied/failed/committed/provider states, tamper attempts by each role and integrity reconciliation.

Reports event/trust matrix, attribution/outcome states, durability and fail policy, precise tamper-evidence guarantee, privacy/query/lifecycle design, failure evidence and remaining adversary/legal assumptions.
Keeps event classes, sink capabilities, integrity controls, retention/holds and sensitive-field classification in governed versioned policy with ownership and provenance rather than code folklore.

scenarios.prompt: A service accepts tenantId and actorId in the request body, commits a privilege change, then best-effort inserts an audit row. A database trigger blocks UPDATE/DELETE and the team calls the trail immutable. Implement a defensible evidence path and guarantee statement.

assertions.criterion: Prohibits secret/raw-payload capture, minimizes or tokenizes PII before ingestion, enforces tenant/purpose/field query authorization, bounds sink backpressure by event class and prevents ordinary retention from deleting scoped held evidence.

Separates append-only/tamper evidence from policy-authorized deletion, legal hold and identity erasure; requires durable pending/reject behavior during sink outage and audits privileged query/detokenization access.
Scans events for secrets/PII, tests cross-tenant and field-level query denial, export bounds, sink outage/backlog/recovery, retention with hold/release/erasure, restore and integrity-gap detection.
Reports rejected/dropped/pending event counts, query and detokenization access, held/deleted evidence and integrity gaps without exposing the protected data itself.

scenarios.prompt: Audit middleware logs full headers and bodies, including reset tokens and OTPs. Tenant admins can search by actor email across all tenants. During sink outage an in-memory queue grows without bound. Retention deletes records even under a legal hold because logs are claimed to be immutable.

assertions.criterion: Uses actual engine/broker/store versions and configuration plus matching official documentation as authority, preserving pins and treating new integrity/storage features as migration scope.
Checks schema/partition and uniqueness support, transactional outbox, broker delivery, object-lock/signing capability, retention/hold deletion, key ownership, replicas/restore and tests together.
Records exact verified capability and threat guarantee and avoids copying current database/cloud API or claiming a universal immutable storage primitive.

scenarios.prompt: The repository pins an older supported database, broker and object-store capability. Current examples use different partition, generated identity, immutable-storage, retention-lock and signing APIs. Migration is outside scope.
